Magnetic electromotive force rotary flying saucer - China patent

#ufotwitter

Patent, filed on October 30, 2009, by inventors Ruan Xiaogang (阮晓钢) and Hou Xuyang (侯旭阳) from Beijing University of Technology, describes a disc-shaped (flying saucer-style) aircraft that uses a magnetically levitated, electrically driven rotor system for propulsion and lift.

Key Innovation

The core of the invention is an integrated magnetic levitation electric power rotor system that combines suspension, drive, and rotation in a compact, frictionless package:

Components:

Magnetic levitation rotor wheel — With blades forming an impeller (inner and outer rings).

Electric power ring (stator) — Generates a rotating magnetic field via controlled current to drive the rotor.

Magnetic levitation shaft — Provides radial suspension (using permanent magnets, electromagnets, or superconductors for repulsive/attractive forces).

Magnetic levitation guide rail — Provides axial suspension (upper/lower grooves).

The rotor wheel "floats" without physical contact, rotating around the shaft under electromagnetic thrust. This eliminates mechanical bearings, reduces weight/volume, improves power efficiency, and minimizes noise/vibration.

Power and Control — Self-contained electromagnetic drive (e.g., like a permanent magnet synchronous motor). A control system manages current for speed and direction.

Anti-Torque Solution

To counteract the reaction torque from a single spinning rotor (which would make the whole saucer spin in the opposite direction), the patent proposes dual rotor configurations:

Coaxial axial stacking (one above the other, rotating in opposite directions or with differential tilt/speed).

Radial nesting (inner and outer rotors, also counter-rotating).

By adjusting relative speeds or directions, the system can cancel torque, control the saucer's overall spin angle/velocity, and manage airflow for better stability and maneuverability.

Advantages Claimed

Compact and lightweight design suitable for the confined space inside a disc shell.

High power conversion efficiency (integrated rotor + power system).

Frictionless operation → reduced wear, noise, vibration, and failure risk.

Easier control of rotation.

Improved safety and energy use.

International Classifications: Primarily under B64C 39/00 (flying saucers/other unconventional aircraft) and electric propulsion categories.

Application filed by Beijing University of Technology
